verdict.rationale: Kimi's API Platform documents organization administration. The Admin API lets admins manage members, invitations, projects and keys, and query audit logs. The console lets them manage members, set project budgets and rate limits, and configure an IP whitelist. Permissions stop at project-level membership rather than per-key or role scopes, and no data policies (retention, training use, data governance) are documented. The evidence covers the developer platform, not the consumer assistant workspace. Missing for 10: role-based permission controls, data-policy controls such as retention and training opt-out, workspace admin for the Kimi assistant/Membership product, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a team-admin, I can manage members, permissions, and data policies for my organization's workspace
